newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Off grades, dust pull down Colombo tea prices.
newsitem.headline: Off grades, dust pull down Colombo tea prices.

text.p: Tea prices eased at the Colombo auction, pulled down by falls in off grades and dust as well as high growns, brokers said on Wednesday.

"The market fell mostly because off grades and dust came down and high growns took a dip towards the end of the sale," said a Forbes and Walker broker. "There was a large quantity of off grades and dust on offer which have a direct impact on the sale average."
The anticipated gross auction average price for the 6.1 million kg on offer fell to 103.95 rupees ($1.80) per kg from 104.43 rupees last week, Forbes and Walker said.
The large quantity of low growns, the mainstay of the Colombo auction, was readily absorbed by buyers, brokers said.
Low growns were fully firm to three rupees dearer while mediums were four to five rupees lower.
Select best Western BOPs and BOPFs gained three to five rupees while all others were four to seven rupees lower.
Nuwara Eliyas sold well though not reaching last week's peak rates, brokers said.
The next auction is on March 11-12 where six million kg will be on offer.
